messages:
marta: Quick sync — proposing we decompose the existing control plane relay into two focused components: a Gateway (public, multi-tenant, handles authn/authz, routing policy) and a per-customer Edge sidecar (runs in customer VPC / on-prem, handles instance identity, egress IP preservation, and local cache). RFC follow-up: want concrete tradeoffs for peering vs private endpoint, the auth handoff, and a safe migration path. TL;DR: small gRPC surface + mTLS + short-lived cert/token exchange.
kevin: +1 to decomposition. Biggest open questions: 1) minimal RPC surface (we should avoid chatty control-plane RPCs), 2) retry/timeout semantics so retries don't amplify load, 3) sticky routing if a sidecar needs to be pinned to a gateway node for session affinity.
sam: For the API I'd model it as unary control RPCs + streaming for model/events. Example: Call(Request) -> stream(Response) for generation; Watch(WatchReq) streaming for model/rollout updates. Keep cache/state in the sidecar, gateway should be horizontally scalable/stateless where possible. Plumb x-request-id, tenant-id, and route-version headers.
anika: Security constraints: we must NOT ship long-lived secret keys across networks. Proposal: bootstrap flow where sidecar proves instance identity (signed statement from instance or cloud provider), gateway mints a short-lived bootstrap token, sidecar exchanges that for ephemeral certs (signed by CP CA). Prefer mTLS and short TTLs. For on-prem, support KMS/HSM-signed CSR flow.
lee: Operational note on preserving customer source IPs: if gateway SNATs, customers lose client IP visibility. Options:
- Peering/hairpin: keep original source IP via routing (good for IP-preservation but scales poorly with hundreds of peers)
- NAT mapping table: gateway preserves an X-Original-Ip mapping table; requires state and added complexity
- VPN/tunnel: enterprise customers get a static egress IP via a dedicated tunnel — simpler but not universal.
Peering complicates routing and adds route churn on scale.
sam: Migration idea: dual-run sidecar -> talk to both old relay and new gateway; use route weight in console to gradually increase gateway traffic. Add a per-request header `x-canary-gateway` to force path for debugging. We'll need rollout flags and metric gates (latency, error-rate, model-output-quality) before cutover.
marta: Sketch of bootstrap/token exchange flow (very small):
```
# sidecar -> gateway
POST /bootstrap { tenant_id, node_id, signed_instance_claim }
-> 200 { bootstrap_token }

# sidecar uses bootstrap_token to request cert
POST /v1/certs { csr } Authorization: Bearer bootstrap_token
-> { cert_pem, ca_chain, expires_in }
```
Important: certs short TTL (~5-15m) and automatic rotation. Add an introspection endpoint for token validation.
kevin: We need revocation plans: short TTLs reduce blast radius but do not replace emergency revoke. Options: CRL/ocsp style or push-based revoke notifications via control plane events to sidecars. Push is faster but couples CP to sidecars.
anika: Also recommend an OIDC-compatible introspection endpoint for integration with enterprise identity. For private deployments, require HSM-backed signing and an admin-initiated revoke API. Audit logging must include tenant-id, node-id, and request hash for forensic purposes.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary deployed gateway:v2-spike -> us-west-2 at 2423456820 :rocket:
lee: For customers who absolutely require fixed egress IPs, VPN/tunnel option is the fastest path to market. We should also prototype a per-tenant NAT mapping for smaller customers as a stop-gap.
marta: Next steps / owners: Kevin to draft proto for the gateway <-> sidecar surface, Sam to build a minimal sidecar spike (bootstrap + cert exchange), Anika to author security requirements and revocation matrix. Schedule quick design review Friday 10:00 PT. I'll open a spike issue and tag owners. (reaction :thumbsup:)
